newsitem.title: CHILE: Los Pelambres raises copper output forecast.
newsitem.headline: Los Pelambres raises copper output forecast.

text.p: Antofagasta Holdings Plc has sold 40 percent of its Los Pelambres copper mine to two Japanese consortia and raised the project's planned output to 260,000 tonnes a year, a company official said.
With the boosted output, Los Pelambres will be one of Chile's four largest copper mines when it comes into full operation in September 1999, the official said.

"This is the first major mine to be built by a private Chilean company and it's also the largest shareholding to be taken by Japanese companies" in Chile's copper industry, said the official, who asked not to be identified.

In the announcement made in London and Tokyo, Antofagasta Holdings and the two Japanese consortia said they signed a letter of intent for the purchase by the consortia of a 40 percent equity interest in Los Pelambres.

The letter of intent also calls for two long-term copper concentrate offtake contracts under which Nippon Mining and Metals Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Materials Corp will buy 250,000 tonnes and 150,000 tonnes, respectively, of copper concentrates a year from Los Pelambres.
"We have a detailed letter of intent," said the official.
The deal, whose price has not been made public, was expected to be signed and approved by all necessary parties by mid-1997, he said.

Antofagasta Holdings is owned by Chile's Luksic group. One of the Japanese consortia is comprised of Nippon, Marubeni Corp and Mitsui & Co Ltd, and the other is made up of Mitsubishi Materials Corp and Mitsubishi Corp, according to a statement on the deal.
Los Pelambres, in northern Chile's fourth region near the Argentine border, was originally slated to produce about 230,000 tonnes of copper a year.

The mine's concentrator, originally set to handle 80,000 tonnes of ore a day, will instead take about 85,000 tonnes under the new plan. The 260,000 tonnes annual production will be contained in about 750,000 tonnes of concentrates.
The deposit holds about 2.4 billion tonnes of copper sulphides at an average metal grade of 0.63, the official said.
